Subject: Request: current subprocessor list + objection window for DPA signing

Hi Irene,

Two quick asks from procurement and legal so we can finish approvals: 1) the most recent subprocessor list (including location/role for each vendor), and 2) the notice/objection timeline Redwood expects once the DPA is signed (our security team wants to confirm we have at least 30 days to review and object if needed).

Tom

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Request: current subprocessor list + objection window for DPA signing

Tom — thanks for the clear asks. Quick responses below and attached materials.

- Subprocessor list: attached CSV (subprocessor_list_20270601.csv) includes vendor, purpose, region, and data access level.
- Objection window: our standard process is a 45-day notification window after the initial subprocessor notice is served. During that window customers may raise objections tied to documented data-protection risks; if objections are raised we engage in the review/escalation process described in the DPA.
- eSign: we will execute the DPA by DocuSign. Ive included an internal checklist and the DocuSign preparation link below; when you confirm the signatories Ill send the envelope.

Attachments: subprocessor_list_20270601.csv, redlines_dpa_v3.docx, esign-instructions.pdf
DocuSign link (prep): https://app.docusign.com/prepare/ABC-123-GBF
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.company.com/deals/GF-2026-0421

If Greenbank needs a firm 30-day requirement instead of 45, we can propose an expedited exception for Dedicated Capacity customers on a case-by-case basis — but that requires internal approval from product/security and a separate addendum. Let me know if you want me to pursue that now.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Privacy & Compliance (Contracts)
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: subprocessor_list_20270601.csv]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: current subprocessor list + objection window for DPA signing

Team — forwarding Greenbank's ask. Key items: they prefer a 30-day objection window; we currently use 45. Theyre ready to sign and want DocuSign link. Can we consider an accelerated path? Options I see:

1) Keep standard 45-day window but offer an expedited review with a guaranteed internal response within 15 business days if they sign a small addendum (tight SLA) — needs security clearance.
2) Make a one-off 30-day exception for this enterprise deal (GF-2026-0421) with product & security sign-off.
3) Keep 45 but offer interim mitigations (e.g., limited subprocessor access until review complete) — operationally heavier.

Please respond with feasibility and suggested language for the DPA notice section. Ive attached our current redlines.

Thanks,
Irene
[Attachment: redlines_dpa_v3.docx]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: current subprocessor list + objection window for DPA signing

Irene — short reply: security prefers keeping 45 as the baseline. Operationally we can commit to an expedited path for high-value customers: if Greenbank signs the execution envelope and returns a signed addendum committing to dedicated-capacity mitigations (where applicable), we can shorten to 30 days and guarantee a formal security response within 15 business days. That gives them what they want while preserving the default for broader customers.

Proposed language snippet (for your edit):
"Notwithstanding the standard forty-five (45) day notice period set forth in Section X, for customers that execute the dedicated-capacity addendum and request expedited review, Redwood will accept written objections within thirty (30) days of notice and provide a formal security response within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of the objection."

Would like Monica to confirm if Legal/Pricing needs any revenue-level threshold or delta in SOW for this to apply.

-Karthik

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@greenbank.com>
Cc: procure@greenbank.com, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: current subprocessor list + objection window for DPA signing

Tom — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per internal alignment, heres what we can do to keep your timeline and preserve our controls:

- Attached is the current subprocessor list (subprocessor_list_20270601.csv).
- Standard notice window: 45 days after notice (this is the baseline in our DPA).
- Expedited option for Greenbank: we can offer a 30-day objection window if Greenbank executes the Dedicated-Capacity Addendum (one-page) and agrees to the expedited-review commitment in writing. If you want to pursue this, I can attach the addendum to the DocuSign envelope.
- DocuSign: Ive prepared the envelope and will send once you confirm signatories. Prepared envelope link: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/ABC-123-GBF

Proposed pick-two sentence for the DPA (final):
"Redwood will provide thirty (30) days for Customer objections to a newly-notified subprocessor where the parties have executed the Dedicated-Capacity Addendum; otherwise, the standard forty-five (45) day notice period shall apply. Upon receipt of a timely objection under the expedited path, Redwood will provide a written security response within fifteen (15) business days and, where reasonable, implement mitigations or engage in joint risk remediation discussions."

Please confirm: 1) the names and emails of the Greenbank signatories for DocuSign, and 2) whether you want the Dedicated-Capacity Addendum included in the envelope. If we dont receive objections within 30/45 days (per the path you pick), the notified subprocessor(s) will be deemed accepted per the DPA language.

If you prefer we can keep the envelope live but add the addendum as an optional signer step so Greenbank can choose during execution.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Head of Privacy & Compliance (Contracts)
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: subprocessor_list_20270601.csv]
